content.content: When invoked as `deccy new -m <summary> --on <id>... [--evaluates <id>...]` with valid ids, the deccy CLI shall write the skeleton with kind decision when the invocation names no `--evaluates` and with kind evaluation when it names one or more. That flag's presence shall be the whole of the selection: every valid invocation falls in exactly one of those two cases, the kind shall not be read from the graph or from the ids the invocation names, no other flag or argument shall name it, and no skeleton element other than the born node's kind shall follow whether `--evaluates` is named.
content.rationale: Kind is what keeps the birth out of the evaluation path; keying the split on whether `--evaluates` is named reads it off the argument surface the invocation already carries, so the kind is a function of the invocation alone — no graph read, no second selector — and every other skeleton element stays where its own decision puts it.
